description: Lightweight Nearest Neighbors with Flexible Backends

summary.one_liner: Vicinity is a lightweight Python vector store that offers one unified interface for nearest neighbor search across many ANN backends, with built-in evaluation of queries per second and recall.
summary.what_it_does: Vicinity builds a vector store from NumPy vectors and arbitrary serializable items, using a single API regardless of the underlying library. It supports top-k queries, threshold queries, and batches of query vectors. Backends include an exact flat index (BASIC), HNSW via hnswlib, USEARCH, ANNOY, PyNNDescent, FAISS (with nine index types), and Voyager. Vector stores can be saved and loaded locally or pushed to and loaded from the Hugging Face Hub. The evaluate method reports queries per second and recall for a chosen backend against the full vector set.
use_cases: compare approximate nearest neighbor libraries on the same data
semantic search over sentence or document embeddings
k-nearest-neighbor lookup with cosine or euclidean distance
benchmark recall and speed of vector indexes
persist a vector index to disk or share it on the Hugging Face Hub
notable: Unified interface over many ANN libraries, so backends can be swapped without relearning APIs
Built-in evaluate method reporting queries per second and recall
BASIC backend supports both insertion and deletion
All nine FAISS index types exposed through one backend option
Optional Hugging Face Hub push and load, with model name stored in metadata
caveats: ANN backends (all except BASIC) do not support dynamic deletion; the index must be rebuilt to remove items
Insertion is only supported for FAISS, HNSW, and USEARCH
Installing specific backends requires separate optional extras
